items.title: Bob Schulz interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: Wynton Marsalis. Thank goodness for him. He’s come along and brought this back and re-introduced it to everyone again

ctx.x: Yeah. Wynton Marsalis. Thank goodness for him. He’s come along and brought this back and re-introduced it to everyone again, and I think the African-Americans are looking at it as cool, but that’s not for me. Let him do it.

Yeah. That’s true. And you wonder sometimes if Buddy Bolden for instance could envision that music that he played on the stage of Lincoln Center, would it be like whoa — because the music came from such a — the word escapes me — a down home source, that it was really pop music, that it was created sometimes by not schooled musicians, and now it’s been elevated to an art form.
